summary: The ellipsoid bonus forward-comm functors always build their buffer view with a row stride of size_forward, but when called from pack_comm_vel_kokkos/unpack_comm_vel_kokkos the buffer stride is size_forward+size_velocity and the offset already includes size_velocity, so the quaternions are written into and read from the wrong buffer rows.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style ellipsoid/kk' with 'comm_modify vel yes' on a GPU build: the ghost quaternions are garbage and the neighbouring atom's communicated x/v are overwritten -> completely wrong aspherical forces, likely blow-up.
suggested_fix: Pass the vel_flag (or the already-computed stride) into the bonus functors and build the buffer view with elements = size_forward + (vel_flag ? size_velocity : 0), matching AtomVecKokkos_PackCommVel.

summary: Source file contains a non-ASCII character (U+2019 RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK) in a comment, violating the project's 7-bit US-ASCII rule and failing the style CI check.
failure_scenario: `cd src && make check` / the style-check.yml GitHub workflow fails on this file before the release.
suggested_fix: Replace the typographic apostrophe with a plain ASCII apostrophe (J's).

summary: AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos silently accepts the 'superellipsoid' sub-style argument but is hard-wired to the plain-ellipsoid bonus layout and never allocates atom->radius, so ellipsoid/kk superellipsoid is broken rather than rejected.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_ellipsoid_kokkos.cpp:39 hard-codes `size_exchange_bonus = 8;` and the pack/unpack bonus functors move exactly shape[3]+quat[4] (lines 483-489, 557-563, 655-661), matching src/atom_vec_ellipsoid.cpp:46-48 size_border_bonus/size_restart_bonus_one = 8.  AtomVecEllipsoid::process_args (src/atom_vec_ellipsoid.cpp:1095-1114) raises those to 13, switches the bonus storage to bonus_super, and appends "radius" to fields_grow/copy/border/border_vel/exchange/restart/create.  AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos does not override process_args, and its grow() (lines 87-99) grows tag,type,mask,image,x,v,f,rmass,angmom,torque,ellipsoid - never atomKK->k_radius - while set_atom_masks() will put RADIUS_MASK into datamask_border, so AtomVecKokkos_PackBorder (atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:1534-1535) reads _radius(j) from an unallocated view.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style ellipsoid/kk superellipsoid' -> null/empty radius view dereferenced during the first borders() call, and blockiness parameters are never communicated -> crash or silently wrong superquadric shapes.
suggested_fix: Override process_args in AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos to error out on 'superellipsoid' (or implement it: grow k_radius, use the 13-wide bonus layout and the Bonus_Super struct).

summary: AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos_PackExchangeBonus reads the bonus array through _bonus while concurrently writing the same memory through the _bonusw alias in the same parallel_for, so a compacted bonus entry can be read after another thread has overwritten it.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_ellipsoid_kokkos.cpp:631-634 aliases the same DualView twice:
      _bonus(bonus.template view<DeviceType>()),
      ...
      _bonusw(bonus.template view<DeviceType>()),
and operator() at lines 655-677 first reads `_bonus(j).shape[0] ... _bonus(j).quat[3]` for j = _ellipsoid[i] and then writes
        _ellipsoidw[_bonus[j_bonus].ilocal] = i_bonus;
        _bonusw[i_bonus] = _bonus[j_bonus];
Nothing orders these across threads.  The authors were aware of the hazard - lines 756-757 say 'must backfill ellipsoid after pack exchange bonus in a separate functor to prevent race conditions' - but the bonus compaction itself was left in the packing kernel.
failure_scenario: Two atoms leaving the sub-domain in the same exchange whose copylist_bonus tail entry for one is the i_bonus slot of the other: the second thread reads a slot the first has already overwritten -> the ellipsoid that stays behind gets the wrong shape/quaternion.  Requires a specific ordering, so it is intermittent.
suggested_fix: Move the bonus compaction (the `_bonusw[i_bonus] = _bonus[j_bonus]` block) into its own parallel_for after the packing kernel, exactly as was done for AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos_BackfillEllipsoid, or verify and document that copylist_bonus can never alias a sent i_bonus.

summary: AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos::sort_kokkos applies the per-atom bin permutation to the bonus array, which is indexed by ellipsoid[i] rather than by atom index, and it uses the d_bonus member that is never assigned anywhere.
failure_scenario: If the bonus guard in AtomKokkos::sort is ever relaxed, an on-device atom sort scrambles shapes/quaternions and leaves stale bonus.ilocal values -> silently wrong aspherical dynamics.
suggested_fix: Remove the `Sorter.sort(..., d_bonus)` call (and the unused d_bonus/h_bonus members), or implement a proper bonus re-index + ilocal fixup before enabling device sorting for bonus styles.

summary: The ellipsoid border-bonus functors index the communication buffer with the raw view's own extent(1) instead of the packing stride size_border(+size_velocity), which disagrees with AtomVecKokkos_UnpackBorderVel when the receive buffer was allocated with the narrower shape.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style ellipsoid/kk' + 'comm_modify vel yes' with more than one MPI rank: unpack_border_bonus_kokkos reads the bonus flag/shape/quat at row-stride 15 from a buffer that unpack_border_vel_kokkos treated as row-stride 21 -> ghost ellipsoid shapes and orientations come from the wrong atom.
suggested_fix: Build an explicit unmanaged view with elements = size_border + (vel_flag ? size_velocity : 0) inside the bonus border functors (and fix grow_recv_kokkos to allocate the wider row when ghost_velocity is set).

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 02
summary: The ellipsoid bonus forward-comm functors build their buffer view with row stride size_forward even when called from the velocity comm path, whose buffer stride is size_forward+size_velocity and whose offset already includes size_velocity, so quaternions land in / are read from the wrong rows.
evidence: atom_vec_ellipsoid_kokkos.cpp:215-218 (elements = size_forward), 239-240 (offset += size_velocity when vel_flag); atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:824-826 uses size_forward + size_velocity for the velocity path.
failure_scenario: atom_style ellipsoid/kk + comm_modify vel yes on a GPU: garbage ghost quaternions and neighboring atoms' x/v overwritten.
suggested_fix: Pass vel_flag into the bonus functors and size the buffer view with size_forward + (vel_flag ? size_velocity : 0).

summary: coeff() bounds the angle type range with atom->ndihedraltypes instead of atom->nangletypes, so coefficients are uploaded for the wrong number of types (out-of-bounds writes or silently missing types).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:300-311: `int ilo,ihi;` / `utils::bounds(FLERR,arg[0],1,atom->ndihedraltypes,ilo,ihi,error);` / `for (int i = ilo; i <= ihi; i++) { k_nterms.view_host()[i] = nterms[i]; ... }`. The CPU base uses the angle type count: src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_gaussian.cpp:208-209: `int ilo, ihi;` / `utils::bounds(FLERR, arg[0], 1, atom->nangletypes, ilo, ihi, error);`. Every sibling in this group also uses nangletypes, e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_charmm_kokkos.cpp:284 `utils::bounds(FLERR,arg[0],1,atom->nangletypes,ilo,ihi,error);`. The dual views being indexed are sized nangletypes+1 (src/KOKKOS/angle_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:65-71, 282-283).
failure_scenario: Any angle-only system (no dihedrals, atom->ndihedraltypes == 0): `angle_style gaussian/kk` + `angle_coeff 1 300.0 2 ...` aborts with the bogus error 'Numeric index 1 is out of bounds (1-0)'. If ndihedraltypes > nangletypes, `angle_coeff * ...` writes k_nterms/k_angle_temperature/k_alpha/k_width/k_theta0 host mirrors past index nangletypes -> heap corruption. If 0 < ndihedraltypes < nangletypes, `angle_coeff * ...` uploads only the first ndihedraltypes types; the remaining types keep nterms==0 on the device, so their Gaussian sum is 0 -> log(0) energy and 0/0 forces.
suggested_fix: Change `atom->ndihedraltypes` to `atom->nangletypes` on line 301 to match AngleGaussian::coeff.

summary: The sum_g_i underflow guard uses SMALLG = 2.3e-308 cast to KK_FLOAT, which becomes exactly 0.0f in single/mixed-precision KOKKOS builds and therefore never fires.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:31 `static constexpr double SMALLG = 2.3e-308;` and :221-223 `// avoid overflow` / `if (sum_g_i < sum_numerator * static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALLG))` / `sum_g_i = sum_numerator * static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALLG);`. KK_FLOAT is `float` for LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE and LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_DOUBLE (src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:399-408), and static_cast<float>(2.3e-308) underflows to 0.0f, so the test degenerates to `if (sum_g_i < 0.0f)`. sum_g_i is then used at :228 `eangle = -kbt * Kokkos::log(sum_g_i);` and :230 `a = -4.0*kbt*(sum_numerator/sum_g_i)*s;`. The CPU base performs the identical guard in double: src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_gaussian.cpp:32 and :135-136.
failure_scenario: Build with -DLMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE (or SINGLE_DOUBLE) and run angle_style gaussian/kk with an angle far from every theta0 (all exponents very negative): every g_i underflows, sum_g_i == 0.0f, the guard does not fire, log(0) gives -inf energy and sum_numerator/sum_g_i gives inf/NaN forces -> NaN trajectory. The double-precision default build is unaffected.
suggested_fix: Evaluate the guard in double (or use a KK_FLOAT-appropriate floor such as Kokkos::Experimental::norm_min_v<KK_FLOAT> / std::numeric_limits<KK_FLOAT>::min()) instead of casting a double-denormal constant to KK_FLOAT.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 00
summary: coeff() bounds the angle type with atom->ndihedraltypes instead of atom->nangletypes (base and every sibling use nangletypes); dual views are sized nangletypes+1.
evidence: angle_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:301 vs src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_gaussian.cpp coeff().
failure_scenario: Angle-only system (ndihedraltypes=0): bogus 'out of bounds (1-0)' error; ndihedraltypes>nangletypes: host-mirror overflow; fewer: types silently left with nterms=0 -> log(0)/NaN.
suggested_fix: Use atom->nangletypes.

summary: MLIAPDummyModelKokkos's destructor decrements the Python unified_interface reference that its base class destructor also decrements, so the object is released twice for a single incref.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:140-145 '~MLIAPDummyModelKokkos() { // manually decrement borrowed reference from Python\n  Py_DECREF(unified_interface); }' -- and the base destructor, which always runs afterwards, does exactly the same: src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified.cpp:123-127 'MLIAPDummyModel::~MLIAPDummyModel() { Py_DECREF(unified_interface); }'. build_unified takes exactly one reference per object: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:251-255 'model->unified_interface = unified_interface; Py_INCREF(unified_interface); descriptor->unified_interface = unified_interface; Py_INCREF(unified_interface);'. The sibling Kokkos descriptor gets this right and deliberately leaves the DECREF to the base: lines 41-45 '~MLIAPDummyDescriptorKokkos() { // done in base class\n  // Py_DECREF(unified_interface); }'.
failure_scenario: 'pair_style mliap/kk unified <module>' followed by redefining pair_style, or simply shutting LAMMPS down: three Py_DECREFs are issued against two Py_INCREFs, dropping the interface object's refcount to zero (or below) while the descriptor still holds a pointer to it -- a use-after-free/abort in CPython, or 'Fatal Python error: deallocating None'-style corruption.
suggested_fix: Delete the Py_DECREF from ~MLIAPDummyModelKokkos() and let MLIAPDummyModel's destructor release the reference, mirroring the descriptor.

summary: MLIAPDummyDescriptorKokkos::set_elements() forgets to set allocated_elements, so the per-element name strings it strdups are never freed.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:122-128 'void MLIAPDummyDescriptorKokkos<DeviceType>::set_elements(char **elems, int nelems) { nelements = nelems; elements = new char *[nelems]; for (int i = 0; i < nelems; i++) { elements[i] = utils::strdup(elems[i]); } }' versus the CPU original src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified.cpp:108-114 which ends with 'allocated_elements = 1;'. The base destructor frees the strings only under that flag: src/ML-IAP/mliap_descriptor.cpp:36-40 'if (allocated_elements) for (int i = 0; i < nelements; i++) delete[] elements[i]; delete[] elements;'.
failure_scenario: Every 'pair_style mliap/kk unified ...' leaks nelements strdup'd strings; repeated pair_style redefinition in a long script leaks steadily.
suggested_fix: Add 'allocated_elements = 1;' at the end of MLIAPDummyDescriptorKokkos::set_elements().

summary: update_pair_energy zeroes the per-atom energy array over nlocal entries although it is allocated with nlistatoms (= list->inum) entries, unlike the CPU version which loops over nlistatoms.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:271-274 'const auto nlocal = data->nlocal; Kokkos::parallel_for(nlocal, KOKKOS_LAMBDA(int ii) { d_eatoms[ii] = 0; });' versus src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified.cpp:244-245 'const auto nlistatoms = data->nlistatoms; for (int ii = 0; ii < nlistatoms; ii++) data->eatoms[ii] = 0;'. eatoms/k_eatoms is created with nlistatoms entries in src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:101-102 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatoms, eatoms, nlistatoms, "mliap_data:eatoms");'. update_atom_energy (line 381) writes d_eatoms[i] over nlocal for the same reason.
failure_scenario: Any configuration where list->inum is smaller than atom->nlocal (a pair_style hybrid sub-list, or a neighbor list restricted to a subset of the atoms) makes the zeroing kernel write past the end of the eatoms device allocation.
suggested_fix: Loop over data->nlistatoms in the zeroing kernel (and bound update_atom_energy the same way), matching the CPU implementation and the allocation size.

summary: ~MLIAPDummyModelKokkos() calls Py_DECREF(unified_interface) and its base ~MLIAPDummyModel() does the same, so the Python object is released twice for one incref.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:144 vs src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified.cpp:126). Note the sibling descriptor destructor at mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:44 has exactly this call commented out, which is the intended fix.

summary: With the device atom map and MAP_ARRAY, the global->local map array is never cleared: exchange_device() skips map_clear() and map_set_device() only clears the hash, so map() returns stale local indices for atom IDs that have migrated off this rank instead of -1.
failure_scenario: GPU run with the defaults (ngpus>0 => atom_map_legacy=0, exchange_comm_legacy=0) and an atom-ID range small enough that map_style is MAP_ARRAY.  An atom whose ID once lived on this rank migrates away; a bonded partner lookup for that ID then returns the stale local index instead of -1, so 'Bond/Angle atom missing' is not detected and neigh_bond builds a bond to an unrelated atom -> silently wrong forces instead of a hard error.
suggested_fix: Either drop the atom_map_legacy guard around map_clear() in exchange_device()/CommTiledKokkos, or add a device-side clear of k_map_array (deep_copy(view_device(),-1)) at the start of AtomKokkos::map_set_device() the way the hash branch already clears d_map_hash.

summary: k_exchange_copylist_bonus is marked modified on the host and synced to the device on every dimension of every exchange, even when there is no bonus data (bonus_flag == 0).
failure_scenario: Any non-bonus atom style: three needless host->device copies of k_exchange_copylist_bonus per exchange() call (once per dimension), plus a modify/sync flag toggle on a view nothing reads.
suggested_fix: Move the modify_host()/sync<DeviceType>() pair inside the 'if (bonus_flag)' block.

summary: grow_send_kokkos() sizes the send buffer with the constant Comm::BUFEXTRA instead of the Comm::bufextra member, so the extra headroom the legacy CommBrick::exchange() relies on (maxexchange + BUFEXTRA) is not provided.
failure_scenario: Legacy exchange path (package kokkos comm no, or gpu/aware off with >1 rank) with a style whose per-atom exchange size is large (many bonds/angles per atom, or fixes contributing a large maxexchange_fix): AtomVec::pack_exchange writes past the end of k_buf_send's host allocation.
suggested_fix: Use the Comm::bufextra member (kept up to date by Comm::init_exchange()) instead of Comm::BUFEXTRA, and round the row count up rather than down when dividing by size_border.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 06
summary: With the device atom map, exchange_device() skips map_clear() (guarded by atom_map_legacy) and map_set_device() clears only the hash, so a MAP_ARRAY map keeps stale local indices for atom IDs no longer on this rank instead of -1.
evidence: comm_kokkos.cpp:1114-1115; atom_map_kokkos.cpp:219-220 clears only d_map_hash; the array branch only writes d_map_array(tag_i)=i for present atoms; src/comm_brick.cpp calls map_clear unconditionally.
failure_scenario: An atom migrates off the rank; a bonded partner lookup for its ID returns a stale index (possibly now a different atom) instead of -1, so 'Bond atoms missing' is not detected and a bond is built to the wrong atom -> silent wrong forces instead of an error.
suggested_fix: Drop the atom_map_legacy guard around map_clear() or deep_copy(k_map_array.view_device(),-1) at the start of map_set_device().

summary: Wrong logical operator in the tmpid skip guard: '(j == 0) && (j < i)' instead of the base class's '(j == 0) || (j < i)', so empty bond slots are no longer skipped and lower-index partners would be processed a second time.
failure_scenario: For the local atom with index i == 0 the sentinel value j == 0 that marks an unused tmpid slot is no longer skipped, so up to MAXSPECBOND(=24) spurious self-pair iterations run per outer pass (currently caught by the following clusterID/x0 equality test, so no wrong numbers today). The guard is also the only protection against double-processing a bond if PairReaxFFKokkos::FindBondSpecies ever stored both directions -- it currently stores only j > i (src/KOKKOS/pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp, TagPairReaxFindBondSpecies: 'if (j < i) continue;'), which is what masks the defect.
suggested_fix: Change '&&' to '||' so the guard matches FixReaxFFSpecies::FindMolecule().

summary: datamask_read/datamask_modify are narrowed from the Fix defaults (ALL_MASK/ALL_MASK) although the inherited post_integrate() can delete atoms via FixReaxFFSpecies::DeleteSpecies(), which rewrites every per-atom array on the host; only DVECTOR_MASK is marked modified, leaving the device copies of x/v/tag/type/image stale.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_reaxff_species_kokkos.cpp:94-95: 'datamask_read = X_MASK | V_MASK | Q_MASK | MASK_MASK | DVECTOR_MASK | TYPE_MASK | RMASS_MASK | TAG_MASK; datamask_modify = DVECTOR_MASK;' (src/fix.cpp:110-111 defaults are 'datamask_read = ALL_MASK; datamask_modify = ALL_MASK;'). src/KOKKOS/modify_kokkos.cpp:266-278 ModifyKokkos::post_integrate() does only 'atomKK->sync(fix->execution_space, fix->datamask_read); ... fix->post_integrate(); ... atomKK->modified(fix->execution_space, fix->datamask_modify);'. FixReaxFFSpecies::post_integrate() -> Output_ReaxFF_Bonds() -> 'if (delflag != NONE && nvalid != -1) DeleteSpecies(Nmole, Nspec);' and DeleteSpecies does 'avec->copy(atom->nlocal - 1, i, 1); atom->nlocal--; ... atom->natoms -= ndel; ... atom->nghost = 0; atom->map_init(); atom->map_set();' (src/REAXFF/fix_reaxff_species.cpp). AtomVecKokkos does not override AtomVec::copy() (src/atom_vec.cpp:269), so the compaction is a pure host-side rewrite of every registered per-atom field.
failure_scenario: fix 1 all reaxff/species/kk 1 1 100 species.out delete del.out masslimit 0 50  under -k on -sf kk: after the first deletion step the device still holds the pre-compaction x/v/tag/type/image (and the old nlocal worth of data), so the next device kernel integrates the wrong atoms -- silently wrong trajectories or a crash.
suggested_fix: Leave datamask_read/datamask_modify at ALL_MASK for this (deliberately kokkosable = 0) fix, or at least add every mask that AtomVec::copy() touches and set datamask_modify = ALL_MASK whenever delflag != NONE.

summary: allocate_kokkos() grows the 2d coefficient DualViews with resize() while host and device are in sync; on a GPU build that resizes the device view and replaces the host mirror with a fresh zero-filled allocation, wiping the coefficients of all previously defined dihedral types.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_spherical_kokkos.cpp:473-485 `} else { k_nterms.resize(n+1); k_Ccoeff.resize(n+1,nterms_max); ... }`; coeff() at :524-538 only refills rows ilo..ihi of the host mirrors before k_*.modify_host() at :540-550.  lib/kokkos/containers/src/Kokkos_DualView.hpp:1027-1029 `if (modified_flags(1) >= modified_flags(0)) resize_on_device(...)` and :1044 `h_view = create_mirror_view(typename t_host::memory_space(), d_view);` -- a new, zero-initialized host allocation with no copy from the old host data.  compute() line 95-105 syncs all views to the device, which equalizes the flags and makes the next resize take the device branch.
failure_scenario: dihedral_style spherical/kk; dihedral_coeff 1 1 <10 args>; run 100; dihedral_coeff 2 2 <20 args>  -> nterms_max grows 1->2, all k_* 2d views resize on device, their host mirrors are zeroed, only row 2 is refilled, and the following sync<DeviceType>() pushes zeros for type 1: type-1 dihedrals silently contribute zero energy and force.
suggested_fix: After a resize, refill the complete host mirror for all types 1..ndihedraltypes from the CPU-side arrays (as read_restart already does), or sync the DualViews to host before resizing so resize takes the host-preserving branch.

summary: The Kokkos kernel does not apply the minimum-image convention to the three bond vectors, while the CPU base style does.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_spherical_kokkos.cpp:248-252 `for (int d = 0; d < g_dim; ++d) { vb12[d] = x(i2,d) - x(i1,d); vb23[d] = ...; vb34[d] = ...; }` with no remapping.  src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/dihedral_spherical.cpp:111-120 does the same subtraction and then `domain->minimum_image(FLERR, vb12[0], vb12[1], vb12[2]); domain->minimum_image(FLERR, vb23[...]); domain->minimum_image(FLERR, vb34[...]);`
failure_scenario: A configuration in which a dihedral bond vector computed from the stored (ghost) coordinates is longer than half a box length: the CPU style remaps it, the /kk style does not, so the two give different phi/theta and different forces.
suggested_fix: Either replicate the minimum-image remapping in the device kernel (using the domain data already exported to Kokkos, cf. other styles), or document/confirm that ghost coordinates make the remapping a no-op and drop it from the CPU style as well.

summary: fix wall/region/kk reads atom radius on the device for the colloid wall style but RADIUS_MASK is not in datamask_read, so the device radius array is never synced.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_region_kokkos.cpp:47 `datamask_read = X_MASK | V_MASK | F_MASK | MASK_MASK;`.  post_force() line 78 syncs only `datamask_read`, then line 98 `if (style == COLLOID) d_radius = atomKK->k_radius.template view<DeviceType>();`.  The kernel reads it at line 164 `tooclose = d_radius(i);` and line 195 `else if (style == COLLOID) engKK = colloid(r,d_radius(i),fwallKK);`.  No other sync in this file covers RADIUS_MASK (only sync call is line 78).  Compare the base FixWallRegion::post_force in src/fix_wall_region.cpp which uses the host `atom->radius` directly.
failure_scenario: `fix wall/region ... colloid ... /kk` on a GPU: radius is filled on the host by read_data/`set diameter`/a non-kk fix and is only copied to the device by an explicit RADIUS_MASK sync.  Without it d_radius contains zeros (or stale values), so `tooclose` is 0 and the colloid wall energy/force uses a wrong particle radius -- wrong forces, and the 'Particle outside surface of region used in fix wall/region' check no longer fires.
suggested_fix: Add RADIUS_MASK to datamask_read (at least when style == COLLOID), e.g. in the constructor after parsing style, or sync it explicitly in post_force before assigning d_radius.

summary: Corrupted GPL license header text: 'the GNU Gdirectoryeneral Public License.'
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_composition_atom_kokkos.cpp:9 '   the GNU Gdirectoryeneral Public License.' vs src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_composition_atom.cpp:9 '   the GNU General Public License.'
failure_scenario: No runtime effect, but the shipped source carries a mangled license notice.
suggested_fix: Restore the standard header line 'the GNU General Public License.'

summary: Local variable 'size_peratom_cols' shadows the Compute base-class member of the same name inside compute_peratom().
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_composition_atom_kokkos.cpp:141 'int size_peratom_cols = 1 + atom->ntypes;' shadows Compute::size_peratom_cols, which the base sets in src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_composition_atom.cpp:60 'size_peratom_cols = 1 + ntypes;'; the device kernel at line 226 uses the member, the allocation at line 145 uses the local.
failure_scenario: Harmless today because both hold 1+atom->ntypes, but any future divergence between the two silently allocates a result array of one width and iterates it with another.
suggested_fix: Delete the local declaration and use the inherited member; likewise drop 'int count = 1.0;' (line 197) in favour of 'int count = 1;'.

summary: The per-type-pair scale[i][j] prefactor of the CPU core/shell style is missing in the KOKKOS port, so 'fix adapt ... pair coul/long/cs scale ...' has no effect with coul/long/cs/kk.
evidence: src/CORESHELL/pair_coul_long_cs.cpp:107 'prefactor = qqrd2e * scale[itype][jtype] * qtmp*q[j];', :138 'forcecoul = scale[itype][jtype] * qtmp*q[j] * table;', :141 and :162 all apply scale (inherited PairCoulLong::extract exposes it to fix adapt).  'grep -n scale src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_long_cs_kokkos.{cpp,h}' returns no hits; compute_fcoul (:229, :244) and compute_ecoul (:294) build prefactor as 'qqrd2e * qtmp*q[j] / reps' with no scale, and params_coul (pair_coul_long_cs_kokkos.h:48-55) stores only cut_coulsq.
failure_scenario: pair_style coul/long/cs/kk with 'fix adapt ... pair coul/long/cs scale ...': the scaling factor is silently ignored and the /kk run diverges from the CPU run.
suggested_fix: Store scale[i][j] in params_coul (filled in init_one) and multiply it into prefactor/forcecoul/ecoul in both branches, as the CPU style does.

summary: coeff() and read_restart() build the coefficient DualViews as function-local temporaries whose host mirrors die at the end of the function, and they copy r0/k2/k3/k4/A/B for ALL types including ones whose coefficients are still uninitialized.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_quartic_exp_kokkos.cpp:243-256 'DAT::tdual_kkfloat_1d k_r0("BondQuarticExp::r0",n+1); ... d_r0 = k_r0.template view<DeviceType>();' - the class (src/KOKKOS/bond_quartic_exp_kokkos.h:85-88) only keeps the d_* device views, no k_* members, and compute() (:84-90) syncs nothing. The same pattern is repeated in read_restart() at :292-304. The fill loop at :257-264 runs 'for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++)' over every type, but BondQuarticExp::allocate() (src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/bond_quartic_exp.cpp:129-134) leaves r0/k2/.../B uninitialized until each type's bond_coeff, unlike every other style in this group which loops only ilo..ihi (cf. bond_class2_kokkos.cpp:252).
failure_scenario: 'bond_coeff 1 ...' with nbondtypes = 2 reads uninitialized heap doubles for type 2 and static_cast<KK_FLOAT>s them; harmless today because type 2 is unusable, but it is undefined behaviour and can raise FP exceptions under -ffpe-trap. It also makes the style unmaintainable: the host mirrors are gone, so a later k_*.sync/modify cannot be added.
suggested_fix: Declare k_r0/k_k2/k_k3/k_k4/k_A/k_B as class members allocated in allocate() (as bond_class2_kokkos does), and restrict the coeff() fill loop to ilo..ihi.

summary: Grid3dKokkos::forward_comm()/reverse_comm() select the brick vs tiled path from the live comm->layout, while the matching data structures were built from the snapshot Grid3d::layout_grid taken at construction, so a layout change during a run makes the two disagree.
failure_scenario: Any sequence where comm->layout flips to LAYOUT_TILED after this Grid3dKokkos was set up but before it is destroyed (e.g. a balance/rcb between the grid setup and the next kspace comm): forward_comm() then takes the tiled branch while nsend/nrecv/ncopy are all still 0 from setup_comm_brick(), so no ghost grid data is exchanged at all and PPPM silently uses stale/zero ghost planes.  Currently masked because fix balance calls kspace->reset_grid() immediately after changing comm->layout.
suggested_fix: Use the inherited layout_grid member in both dispatchers (and fix the misleading indentation of the if/else while there).

summary: fix temp/csld/kk draws its random velocities from a Kokkos random pool but inherits the base class write_restart/restart, which save and restore only the unused RanMars generator - so a restarted run replays the same random-velocity sequence from the beginning instead of continuing the stream.
evidence: fix_temp_csld_kokkos.cpp:45-49 seeds 'rand_pool(utils::inumeric(FLERR, arg[6], false, lmp) + comm->me)' and the kernel draws from it (fix_temp_csld_kokkos.cpp:211-215 'rand_type rand_gen = rand_pool.get_state(); ... rand_gen.normal() ...').  The class overrides only the constructor, destructor, init(), end_of_step() and temp_scalar() (fix_temp_csld_kokkos.h:42-56), so src/EXTRA-FIX/fix_temp_csld.cpp:294-329 remain in force: write_restart does 'random->get_state(state); MPI_Gather(...)' and restart does 'random->set_state(list+2+comm->me*103)' on the RanMars object that the Kokkos path never advances.  Nothing re-seeds or restores rand_pool, which is reconstructed from arg[6]+comm->me on every read_restart.
failure_scenario: run 10000 steps with 'fix temp/csld/kk', write_restart, read_restart and continue: the thermostat's gaussian velocity draws restart at the head of the same stream the first run used, so the two segments of the trajectory share identical noise, unlike the CPU 'fix temp/csld' whose RanMars state is restored.  (A second, smaller inconsistency: restart() reads 'list+2+comm->me*103' while write_restart strides by PRNGSIZE = 103, so the two agree only by coincidence of that constant.)
suggested_fix: Override write_restart()/restart() to save and restore the Kokkos pool state (or at minimum document in doc/src/fix_temp_csld.rst that the /kk variant does not restore its random-number state).

summary: For a special-bonded pair the CPU core/shell style rescales r2inv with EPS_EWALD_SQR and uses that rescaled r2inv for the LJ force/energy as well; the Kokkos compute_fpair/compute_evdwl only add EPSILON, so the LJ term diverges from the CPU style at very small separations.
evidence: src/CORESHELL/pair_lj_cut_coul_long_cs.cpp:126 sets `r2inv = 1.0/(rsq + EPS_EWALD_SQR);` inside the `factor_coul < 1.0` branch, and lines 153-157 then use exactly that r2inv for `r6inv = r2inv*r2inv*r2inv; forcelj = r6inv*(lj1*r6inv - lj2);` and `fpair = (forcecoul + factor_lj*forcelj) * r2inv`. src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_long_cs_kokkos.cpp:200-210 instead always uses `const KK_FLOAT rsq = rsq_in + EPSILON; const KK_FLOAT r2inv = 1.0/rsq;` (EPSILON = 1e-20, EPS_EWALD_SQR = 1e-12) and the same in compute_evdwl at lines 296-299.
failure_scenario: A core/shell pair at r ~ 0 with a non-zero special_lj factor: CPU evaluates r6inv from 1/(rsq+1e-12) while the Kokkos style evaluates it from 1/(rsq+1e-20), producing LJ forces/energies that differ by ~24 orders of magnitude (and overflow to inf/NaN under a KK_FLOAT=float build).
suggested_fix: Pass factor_coul into the LJ helpers (or precompute) so compute_fpair/compute_evdwl use 1/(rsq+EPS_EWALD_SQR) when factor_coul < 1.0 and rsq < cut_coulsq, matching the CPU style.
